stops.blurb: Haneda Airport is Tokyo's close-in international gateway, consistently ranked among the world's cleanest and most punctual airports, with Terminal 3 handling international flights just 30 minutes from the city centre.

stops.title: Sumo wrestling experience
stops.notes: approximate — venue not named; Ryogoku Kokugikan area
stops.blurb: Ryogoku is the historic heartland of sumo, home to the Kokugikan national stadium and the training stables where visitors can watch wrestlers' intense morning practice.

stops.title: Asakusa and Senso-ji Temple
stops.blurb: Senso-ji is Tokyo's oldest temple, founded in 628 AD and dedicated to the bodhisattva Kannon, famed for the giant red lantern of its Kaminarimon gate.

stops.title: Free time on Nakamise Shopping Street
stops.blurb: Nakamise is the centuries-old shopping street leading to Senso-ji, lined since the Edo period with nearly a hundred stalls selling traditional snacks, crafts and souvenirs.

stops.title: Skytree base & Solamachi — no ascent
stops.notes: Ground level only — Solamachi mall + looking up. We go UP the tower on Day 15 night (1 Jan). Skip the ticket queue today.
stops.blurb: Tokyo Skytree is Japan's tallest structure at 634 metres, a broadcasting tower with twin observation decks offering panoramic views across the Kanto plain to Mt. Fuji.

stops.title: Kabukiza facade photo
stops.notes: exterior only, 15–20 min; walk Harumi-dori to the Ginza spine
stops.blurb: Kabuki-za (Kabukiza Theatre) is a historic performing arts venue in Tokyo's Ginza district dedicated to traditional Japanese Kabuki theater.

stops.title: G.Itoya flagship — quick hit
stops.notes: Sun 10:00–19:00; 25 min on floors 1–2 — full 12-floor browse on 2 Jan
stops.blurb: G.Itoya is Ginza's legendary stationery emporium, founded in 1904, whose 12-floor flagship is a pilgrimage site for pens, paper and fine Japanese writing goods.

stops.title: Wako Seiko clock tower — 10:30 chime
stops.notes: Westminster chime on the hour since 1954 — photo at the crossing, 1 min to museum
stops.blurb: The Wako building's Seiko clock tower, rebuilt in 1932, is the defining landmark of Ginza's 4-chome crossing, sounding Westminster chimes on the hour since 1954.

stops.title: Seiko Museum Ginza
stops.notes: opens 10:30 (NOT 10:00) — free, reserve the first slot online; 45 min
stops.blurb: The Seiko Museum Ginza traces the watchmaker's history from founder Kintaro Hattori's 1881 shop, displaying Japan's first wristwatches and the Grand Seiko lineage.

stops.title: Seiko Dream Square — buy his SARJ011
stops.notes: Core Shop exclusive; tax-free ≈¥145,000; 60 min incl. paperwork
stops.blurb: Seiko Dream Square is the brand's flagship boutique steps from the Ginza crossing, showcasing the full Seiko and Grand Seiko collections including shop-exclusive models.

stops.title: Kimuraya Honten — warm 1874 anpan
stops.notes: anpan invented here 1874 (~¥200); eat walking the car-free Chuo-dori (Sun 12:00–17:00)
stops.blurb: Ginza Kimuraya is the bakery that invented the anpan — a sake-yeast bun filled with sweet red-bean paste — in 1874, later presented to the Emperor.

stops.title: NISSAN CROSSING (optional, 10 min)
stops.notes: free 2-floor showroom on the same corner — Formula E GEN3 Evo (Tokyo E-Prix livery) + GT-R T-spec; exhibits rotate — only if ahead of schedule, Bic by 12:40
stops.blurb: Nissan Crossing is the carmaker's glassy two-floor brand showroom on Ginza's 4-chome crossing, displaying rotating concept, racing and heritage cars.

stops.title: Bic Camera Yurakucho — her Orient Star
stops.notes: first choice: RK-ND0023L Yukiakari, limited 100 — call ahead; tax-free queue ~10 min
stops.blurb: Bic Camera Yurakucho is a vast multi-floor electronics megastore whose watch department carries major Japanese brands including Seiko and Orient Star at tax-free prices.

stops.title: Lunch — Tricolore Honten (est. 1936)
stops.notes: no bookings, 10–25 min Sunday wait; vegetarian-workable; backup: Café Paulista (1911)
stops.blurb: Tricolore Honten, founded in 1936, is a classic Showa-era Ginza kissaten known for its antique interior, hand nel-dripped coffee and famous eclair.

stops.title: UNIQLO Ginza — 12-floor flagship
stops.notes: hard stop 14:55 → Ginza Stn A2 → Ginza line to Shibuya (~16 min)
stops.blurb: UNIQLO Ginza is the brand's 12-floor global flagship and one of the world's largest UNIQLO stores, stocking flagship-exclusive lines and the full UT collection.

stops.title: Shibuya Sky — sunset slot
stops.notes: ~¥2,600 pp; tickets ~6 Dec 00:00 JST; sunset 16:32
stops.blurb: Shibuya Sky is the 229-metre open-air observatory atop Shibuya Scramble Square, looking straight down on the world's busiest pedestrian crossing.

stops.title: Hachiko + Shibuya Crossing
stops.notes: the Scramble is right here — Starbucks Tsutaya 2F / Mag's Park for the overhead shot
stops.blurb: The Hachiko statue honours the Akita dog who waited at Shibuya Station daily for nine years after his owner's death, beside the famous scramble crossing.

stops.title: Tokyo DisneySea experience
stops.blurb: Tokyo DisneySea is a nautical-themed Disney park found only in Tokyo, widely regarded as one of the most beautifully designed theme parks in the world.

stops.title: Private transfer to Arakurayama Sengen Park
stops.blurb: Arakurayama Sengen Park is a hillside shrine park in Fujiyoshida whose pagoda-and-Mt.-Fuji panorama is one of Japan's most famous postcard views.

stops.title: Chureito Pagoda, Mt. Fuji views
stops.notes: approximate — pagoda sits ~400 steps uphill within Arakurayama Sengen Park
stops.blurb: The Chureito Pagoda is a five-storey vermilion pagoda whose terrace frames Mt. Fuji in Japan's classic postcard composition, reached by a climb of about 400 steps.

stops.title: Lake Kawaguchi sightseeing boat experience
stops.notes: approximate — Funatsu pier next to the Kawaguchiko ropeway
stops.blurb: Lake Kawaguchi is the most accessible of the Fuji Five Lakes, and its sightseeing cruise offers sweeping water-level views of Mt. Fuji from the northern foothills.

stops.title: Oishi Park — sunrise Fuji light
stops.blurb: Oishi Park on Lake Kawaguchi's northern shore is celebrated for its unobstructed lake-and-Fuji panorama, among the finest viewpoints in the Fuji Five Lakes region.

stops.notes: en-route leg
stops.blurb: Kawaguchiko Station is the gateway terminus of the Fuji Five Lakes region, linked to Tokyo by the direct Fuji Excursion limited express and highway buses.

stops.title: Hokuriku Shinkansen Tokyo → Kanazawa
stops.blurb: The Hokuriku Shinkansen is the bullet-train line linking Tokyo with the Japan Sea coast, reaching Kanazawa in about two and a half hours at up to 260 km/h.

stops.title: Kanazawa hotel check-in
stops.notes: hotel TBD — extension ask; placeholder near Kanazawa Station

stops.title: Kenrokuen — yukitsuri snow-ropes
stops.blurb: Kenrokuen is one of Japan's three great landscape gardens, famed in winter for yukitsuri — conical rope supports that protect its ancient pines from heavy snow.

stops.title: Higashi Chaya district stroll
stops.blurb: Higashi Chaya is Kanazawa's largest preserved geisha district, its Edo-period wooden teahouses now housing gold-leaf shops and cafes along lantern-lit lanes.

stops.title: Dinner + Christmas illuminations, Katamachi
stops.blurb: Katamachi is Kanazawa's main shopping and nightlife district, whose landmark Christmas tree illumination doubles as a yukitsuri light display through the winter.

stops.title: Check-out — bags to bell desk
stops.notes: leave bags at the bell desk or station coin lockers (on the way) — no backtracking after breakfast

stops.title: Omicho Market crab breakfast
stops.notes: many crab stalls open 08:00; kobako-gani runs ¥5,000–12,000 for two
stops.blurb: Kanazawa’s 300-year-old covered market — winter snow-crab season at its peak in late December.

stops.title: Train to Kyoto (Tsuruga Shinkansen + Thunderbird)
stops.notes: ~1h45–2h; grab bags en route to the platform
stops.blurb: The Hokuriku extension plus the Thunderbird limited express — Kanazawa to Kyoto in under two hours.

stops.title: Kimono rental & fitting
stops.notes: WEAR YOUR DINNER OUTFIT HERE — shops locker your clothes while you’re in kimono; no hotel detour needed later
stops.blurb: Dressing in a rental kimono for an afternoon in the old lanes is one of Kyoto’s signature experiences.

stops.title: Kiyomizu-dera + Sanneizaka — in kimono, in daylight
stops.notes: moved BEFORE tea (Dec sunset 16:48) — golden-hour photos and the Sanneizaka shops still open
stops.blurb: Kyoto’s great wooden-stage temple above the city, reached through the preserved slope lanes of Sanneizaka.

stops.title: Tea ceremony — warm, indoors at dusk
stops.notes: ASK JAY to rebook the tea slot from 14:50 to ~16:15 — indoors right as the light goes
stops.blurb: A traditional tea ceremony: whisked matcha, seasonal sweets, and the quiet choreography of the tea room.

stops.title: Return kimono — back in dinner clothes
stops.notes: undressing takes 15–20 min; you leave already dressed for dinner

stops.title: Taxi to Hotel Okura (~10 min)
stops.notes: breathe in the lobby before dinner

stops.title: Cathedral Christmas gathering (optional)
stops.notes: 400 m from the Okura — catch the opening carols, walk back for dinner
stops.blurb: A free pre-mass community celebration with carols and handbells at Kyoto’s cathedral, five minutes from the Okura.

stops.title: Christmas-Eve dinner — BOOKED
stops.place: Hotel Okura Kyoto — Sky Restaurant Pittoresque
stops.notes: Menu de Noël ¥20,000–30,000 pp incl. service — book NOW + vegetarian request in writing; 17th floor, city lights below
stops.blurb: Japan’s Christmas Eve ritual at its best: a French course dinner above the lights of Kyoto.

stops.title: Midnight Mass — Kawaramachi Cathedral
stops.notes: Japan’s ‘midnight’ mass runs ~21:00–22:15 — 5 min walk; non-Christians welcome, arrive early; confirm +81 75-231-4785. (Station lights tonight impossible — they’re slotted tomorrow 17:15.)
stops.blurb: Kyoto’s main Catholic cathedral, whose candlelit Christmas Eve services draw a full house each 24 December.

stops.title: JR Nara Line to Inari Station
stops.blurb: Inari Station on the JR Nara Line sits directly opposite the first torii gate of Fushimi Inari Taisha, just two stops from Kyoto Station.

stops.title: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine
stops.blurb: Fushimi Inari Taisha is the head shrine of the rice deity Inari, famed for nearly ten thousand vermilion torii gates tunnelling up its sacred mountain.

stops.title: Sanjusangendo Temple & Kennin-ji Temple visit
stops.notes: Kennin-ji Temple is at 35.0004, 135.7735
stops.blurb: Sanjusangendo houses 1,001 gilded statues of Kannon in Japan's longest wooden hall, while nearby Kennin-ji, founded in 1202, is Kyoto's oldest Zen temple.

stops.title: Gion Hanamikoji Street & Shirakawa Canal stroll
stops.notes: Shirakawa Canal (Gion Shirakawa) is at 35.0064, 135.7747
stops.blurb: Hanamikoji is the signature street of Gion, Kyoto's most famous geisha district, lined with centuries-old wooden ochaya teahouses where geiko and maiko still entertain.

stops.title: City bus / subway to Kyoto Station
Kyoto Station lights — staircase show + tree
stops.notes: final day of the display (runs to 22:00); watch one staircase LED cycle before the 18:00 train
stops.blurb: Kyoto Station’s 171-step grand staircase becomes a giant LED canvas each December, crowned by the station’s Christmas tree.

stops.title: Dinner — Kyoto Ramen Koji (Station 10F)
stops.notes: You're already at the station for the lights — ten regional ramen shops one escalator up. Or swap for the 19:00 daiku concert (see day flag).

stops.title: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) visit
stops.blurb: Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion, is a Zen temple whose top two floors are entirely covered in gold leaf, shimmering above its mirror pond since 1397.

stops.title: Ryoan-ji Zen rock garden visit
stops.blurb: Ryoan-ji holds Japan's most famous Zen rock garden — fifteen stones in raked white gravel, arranged so no single viewpoint reveals all of them at once.

stops.title: Togetsukyo Bridge stroll
stops.blurb: Togetsukyo, the 'Moon Crossing Bridge', has spanned the Katsura River for some four centuries and is the defining landmark of Kyoto's Arashiyama district.

stops.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove walk
stops.blurb: The Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is Kyoto's famed walking path through soaring green bamboo, whose creaking stalks are officially listed among Japan's 100 soundscapes.

stops.title: JR Special Rapid Service, Kyoto Station → Osaka Station
stops.notes: departs Kyoto Station (34.9858, 135.7585)
stops.blurb: The JR Special Rapid Service is the fast conventional train of the Kyoto-Osaka corridor, covering the distance in about 29 minutes with no reservation needed.

stops.title: JR Osaka Loop Line to Osaka Castle
Osaka Castle main keep visit
stops.blurb: Osaka Castle was built by unifier Toyotomi Hideyoshi in the 1580s as Japan's mightiest fortress; its rebuilt keep now houses a museum of the samurai era.

stops.title: Free time around Osaka Station / Grand Front Osaka
stops.blurb: Grand Front Osaka is the flagship shopping and dining complex of the redeveloped Umeda district, packed with showrooms, boutiques and restaurants beside Osaka Station.

stops.title: Umeda Sky Building & Kuchu Teien Observatory
stops.blurb: The Umeda Sky Building is a twin-tower landmark joined at the top by the Kuchu Teien 'Floating Garden' observatory, an open-air rooftop ring 173 metres up.

stops.title: Osaka Station City stroll
stops.blurb: Osaka Station City is the vast station complex at Umeda, uniting department stores, cinemas and rooftop plazas beneath a dramatic 180-metre glass dome roof.

stops.title: Yodobashi Umeda — Seiko & Orient Star
stops.notes: watch buying stop; 09:30–22:00; 2nd pass possible 28 Dec 09:30
stops.blurb: Yodobashi Umeda is one of Japan's largest electronics megastores, its watch floor stocking the full Seiko and Orient Star ranges alongside eight storeys of gadgets.

stops.title: JR Yumesaki Line to Universal-City Station
Walk to USJ main gate
stops.notes: approximate — gate area between Universal-City Station and park

stops.title: Universal Studios Japan full-day experience
stops.blurb: Universal Studios Japan is Osaka's blockbuster theme park, home to Super Nintendo World and the Wizarding World of Harry Potter.

stops.title: Return to Hotel Granvia Osaka via JR Line
Kuromon Ichiba seafood market stroll
stops.blurb: Kuromon Ichiba, known as 'Osaka's kitchen', is a nearly 200-year-old covered market of some 150 stalls grilling scallops, crab and wagyu for strolling eaters.

stops.title: Dotonbori Canal & Shinsaibashi walk
stops.notes: Shinsaibashi shopping street is at 34.6739, 135.5012
stops.blurb: Dotonbori is Osaka's neon-lit canalside entertainment district, famed for the Glico running-man sign and giant mechanical crab, with the Shinsaibashi shopping arcade running north.

stops.title: Shinsekai Hondori Shopping Street stroll
stops.blurb: Shinsekai is Osaka's nostalgic early-1900s entertainment district, a retro warren of kushikatsu skewer joints and glowing signage beneath Tsutenkaku Tower.

stops.title: Tsutenkaku Tower visit
stops.blurb: Tsutenkaku is Shinsekai's beloved retro tower, a 1956 rebuild of a Paris-inspired 1912 original, with the lucky Billiken statue on its observation deck.

stops.title: Tokaido Shinkansen Shin-Osaka → Tokyo
stops.notes: reserve 30 Nov — U-turn rush
stops.blurb: The Tokaido Shinkansen, opened in 1964, is the world's first high-speed railway, whisking passengers between Osaka and Tokyo in about two and a half hours.

stops.title: Tokyo hotel luggage drop
stops.notes: extension night — Jay to quote; placeholder near Tokyo Station

stops.title: Marunouchi + Hibiya illuminations walk
stops.blurb: Marunouchi Naka-dori is Tokyo's elegant tree-lined boulevard beside the station, whose champagne-gold winter illumination of over a million LEDs adjoins the Hibiya district's displays.

stops.title: Nakano Broadway — optional vintage safari
stops.notes: optional; call Jack Road 03-3386-9399; building closes Jan 1
stops.blurb: Nakano Broadway is Tokyo's legendary subculture mall, a 1966 arcade crammed with anime collectibles, manga and some of the city's best vintage-watch dealers.

stops.title: Lazy lunch + afternoon rest
stops.notes: Nothing scheduled all day on purpose — tonight runs past midnight. Tokyo Tower comes free as the lit backdrop at Zojoji.

stops.title: Zojoji Temple — joya-no-kane + midnight, Tokyo Tower backdrop
stops.blurb: Zojoji is the Tokugawa shoguns' family temple, founded in 1393, whose forecourt beneath the lit Tokyo Tower is the classic stage for New Year's Eve bell-ringing.

stops.title: Meiji Jingu — hatsumode via forest approach
stops.notes: 1.5–2 h queue expected
stops.blurb: Meiji Jingu is Tokyo's grandest Shinto shrine, enshrining Emperor Meiji within a 100,000-tree planted forest and drawing Japan's largest hatsumode crowds each New Year.

stops.title: Tokyo Skytree — first night view
stops.notes: ¥3,100 advance; open to 22:00. The ascent we saved — Day 2 was base-only, tonight is the first view from the deck.
stops.blurb: Tokyo Skytree is Japan's tallest structure at 634 metres, a broadcasting tower with twin observation decks offering panoramic views across the Kanto plain to Mt. Fuji.

stops.title: Imperial Palace Ippan Sanga — Nijubashi Main Gate
stops.notes: 2027 notice due late Dec
stops.blurb: Ippan Sanga is one of only two days a year the Imperial Palace's inner grounds open, as the Emperor and family greet the public from the Chowa-den balcony.
